title: TCS Says Eighty Percent of New Hires Will Bring AI Skills
excerpt: India's largest IT services company says four in five new hires will have digital and AI skills, after AI-led work reached 10% of September-quarter revenue.
body:
• TCS says about 80% of its new hires going forward will have digital and artificial intelligence skills, COO Arathi Subramanian told PTI.
  • Of the 4,500 employees added in the September quarter, 25 to 30% were pure AI hires and about 80% were new-age hires overall.
  • AI-led work accounted for 10% of TCS revenue in the September quarter, and the company expects larger AI deal volumes to support margins.
  • TCS onboarded 10,000 freshers in the quarter and about 24,000 in the first half of FY27, according to The People's Board.

Tata Consultancy Services will hire for artificial intelligence first. About 80% of the company's new hires going forward will be people with digital and AI skills, chief operating officer Arathi Subramanian told the Press Trust of India in Mumbai on 12 October, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The comments followed TCS's September-quarter earnings announcement on 8 October, in which AI-led work accounted for 10% of overall revenue.

What TCS announced

Subramanian said the hiring mix seen in the September quarter is the template. Of the 4,500 employees added in the quarter, 25 to 30% were pure AI hires, and about 80% in total were new-age hires. Asked whether that proportion would continue, she said it would, and added that the required talent is available in the market. TCS will also keep investing in niche talent, chief executive and managing director K Krithivasan said, with mergers, acquisitions and partnerships as other areas of investment.

The hiring shift follows the revenue shift. With AI-led work at 10% of revenue in the September quarter, TCS said a rising share of AI revenue should help expand profit margins, which remain below its aspirational levels. Krithivasan said that as AI deal volumes increase, investors would see a margin benefit. The company put total contract value for the quarter at $9.6 billion, and said it is conservative in classifying a deal as an AI deal, while some aspect of AI is present in virtually all the work it is doing.

Freshers and lateral hires

The announcement does not close the door on campus hiring. TCS onboarded 10,000 freshers in the September quarter and roughly 24,000 freshers in the first half of FY27, according to The People's Board, which put the company's workforce at close to 598,000 employees at the start of the fiscal year. The change is in what those hires are expected to bring: four out of five new entrants are now expected to arrive with digital and AI capability rather than acquire it several quarters into the job.

Nor is the advantage limited to fresh graduates. Asked whether AI-native freshers had an edge over mid-career professionals, Subramanian said the advantage belongs to people willing to unlearn and learn. Krithivasan added that a mid-level engineer who is willing to learn has a significant advantage because that engineer already understands the technology landscape and the business domain, which a junior engineer may not. Recent deal wins involving Porsche and Best Buy, where TCS absorbs client staff, were described by Krithivasan as opportunities to help customers transform and become AI-first, not as a sign of market weakness.

What it means for jobseekers

For Indian technology jobseekers, the practical reading is narrow and specific. TCS, the country's largest IT services company, is signalling that AI, cloud, data and cybersecurity-adjacent skills are now the default hiring filter, not a specialist track. Candidates without those skills are competing for a shrinking share of openings: on the company's own numbers, only about one in five new hires falls outside the new-age category. At the same time, executives described demand starting small and expanding: Subramanian said customers sign up for an AI deal in one vertical and then ask for expansion into other areas once the spending proves effective.

What to watch next

The test is whether the 80% mix holds in the December quarter's hiring numbers, and whether peers report the same pattern. Also worth watching is whether AI revenue rises above the 10% share reported for the September quarter, since TCS has tied that growth directly to margin expansion. For experienced engineers, the company's message was explicit: domain knowledge plus new AI skills is the combination it values most.
